title: Additive generators of the maximal-order algebra at a projective point
statement:
Let $k$ be any field, let $N\ge1$, and give $P=k[Z_1,\ldots,Z_N]$ its grading with all variables in degree one [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset P$ be a homogeneous prime ideal not containing $P_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}P_d$. In the ordinary localization $P_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], put
$$U_d=\{f\in P_d:f/1\in(\mathfrak qP_{\mathfrak q})^d\},\qquad U=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}U_d\subseteq P.$$
Here the direct sum denotes finite sums of homogeneous polynomials in the indicated subspaces, and $U_0=k$. Let $T$ consist of the homogeneous elements $t\in U_d$, $d>0$, that satisfy the polynomial identity
$$t(Z+W)=t(Z)+t(W)$$
in the polynomial ring on two disjoint tuples of variables. Then $U$ is a graded $k$-subalgebra of $P$ and $U=k[T]$, where $k[T]$ denotes the subalgebra consisting of polynomial expressions over $k$ in finitely many members of $T$.

source.place: Hironaka, Additive groups associated with points of a projective space, Theorem 2; concrete order-algebra formulation read in Dietel, A refinement of Hironaka’s additive group schemes for an extended invariant (2014), Definition 9.1.3 and Lemma 9.1.4, pp.107–108, https://d-nb.info/1068056037/34. Archival copy WANTED. ILO VIII 2.3.13, p.94, is only the ancestor motivation; no Stacks tag states this theorem.

proof.text: Put $A=P_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak qA$, using [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Each $U_d$ is a $k$-vector subspace, since it is the inverse image of the ideal $\mathfrak m^d$ under the linear map $P_d\to A$. Constants give $U_0=k$. If $f\in U_d$ and $g\in U_e$, then $fg$ is homogeneous of degree $d+e$ by [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra] and $(fg)/1\in\mathfrak m^d\mathfrak m^e=\mathfrak m^{d+e}$. Thus the finite sums defining $U$ form a graded $k$-subalgebra of $P$.

proof.text: For a multiindex $B\in\mathbf N^N$ write $|B|=\sum_i B_i$ and define $D_B f=[W^B]f(Z+W)$ by coefficient extraction in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Expanding monomials gives $D_B(Z^E)=\binom EB Z^{E-B}$ when $B\le E$ componentwise, and zero otherwise, where $\binom EB=\prod_i\binom{E_i}{B_i}$ is interpreted in $k$. Multiplying the two finite expansions gives $D_B(gh)=\sum_{C\le B}D_C(g)D_{B-C}(h)$. Consequently $D_0$ is the identity and $[D_B,g]=\sum_{0<C\le B}D_C(g)D_{B-C}$, so induction on $|B|$ shows that $D_B$ has differential order at most $|B|$ in the commutator definition of [lem-trf-differential-operator-localization]. Finite sums and multiplication of the output by an element do not increase this order: commute once and induct on the order. Applying that node with $R=k$, $B=P$ and prime $\mathfrak q$ gives an extension $\widetilde D_B:A\to A$ of the same order.

proof.text: For an ideal $I$ in any commutative algebra $C$, a differential operator $E:C\to C$ of order at most $r$ satisfies $E(I^d)\subseteq I^{\max(d-r,0)}$. Here is the elementary commutator induction, with the order convention of [lem-trf-differential-operator-localization]. At $r=0$, $E$ is multiplication by $E(1)$, so preserves every ideal power. At $r>0$, the claim for $d\le r$ merely says the output lies in $C$. For $d>r$, write a generator of $I^d$ as $ab$, with $a\in I$ and $b\in I^{d-1}$. The identity $E(ab)=aE(b)+[E,a](b)$ puts both summands in $I^{d-r}$: use induction on $d$ for the first and on $r$ for the second. Additivity handles sums of these generators. This proves the assertion by induction on $r$, and then on $d$ for each fixed $r$.

proof.text: Take $I=\mathfrak m$ and the localized operators of step 2. For homogeneous $f\in U_d$ and $|B|\le d$, steps 2--3 give $(D_Bf)/1\in\mathfrak m^{d-|B|}$, since the extension agrees on $f/1$. The monomial formula makes $D_Bf$ homogeneous of degree $d-|B|$, so $D_Bf\in U_{d-|B|}$. For $|B|>d$ it is zero. Thus $U$ is stable under all $D_B$, including those of order divisible by the characteristic; no factorial is divided out.

proof.text: Let $K=k[T]\subseteq U$. Since every generator in $T$ is homogeneous, grouping the monomials in any polynomial expression in these generators by total weighted degree shows $K=\bigoplus_d K_d$, where $K_d=K\cap P_d$ [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. Suppose $K\ne U$ and choose the least $d$ with $K_d\ne U_d$. Constants lie in $K$ because it is a $k$-subalgebra, and every element of $U_1$ is additive and hence belongs to $T$ (including the zero polynomial). Thus $K_0=U_0=k$ and $K_1=U_1$, so $d\ge2$. Order degree-$d$ monomials lexicographically. Gaussian elimination in the finite-dimensional space $P_d$ provides a basis of $K_d$ with distinct leading exponents. Subtract multiples of its rows from an element of $U_d\setminus K_d$, starting at the largest pivot. This gives $f\in U_d\setminus K_d$ whose coefficient at every leading exponent of a nonzero element of $K_d$ is zero. There are finitely many degree-$d$ monomials, so this elimination terminates; all row subtractions stay in $U_d$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring].

source.place: Tag 0G36 for localization; explicit coefficient argument by the worker, compared with online Dietel (2014), Lemma 9.1.4 and Proposition 3.4.3(ii)--(iv), printed pp.108 and 43. Archival Dietel copy WANTED.

proof.text: This $f$ cannot be additive, since then $f\in T\subset K$. Hence at least one monomial with nonzero coefficient in $f$ is not additive. Choose its lexicographically largest exponent $E$. Mixed terms $Z^C W^B$ arising from different monomials have different sums $B+C$, so they cannot cancel across exponents. Nonadditivity of $Z^E$ means that $(Z+W)^E-Z^E-W^E$ has a nonzero coefficient. Thus there are nonzero multiindices $B,C$ with $B+C=E$, $0<|B|,|C|<d$, and $\binom EB\ne0$ in $k$; also $\binom EC=\binom EB$. For every additive monomial of degree $d$, both $D_B$ and $D_C$ vanish, because its addition identity has no mixed coefficient of either of these proper degrees. These assertions are direct coefficient comparisons in the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring].

source.place: Tag 0G36 for localization; explicit coefficient argument by the worker, compared with online Dietel (2014), Lemma 9.1.4 and Proposition 3.4.3(ii)--(iv), printed pp.108 and 43. Archival Dietel copy WANTED.

proof.text: Using the extensions of [lem-trf-differential-operator-localization] and the bound of steps 3--4, $D_Bf$ and $D_Cf$ belong to $U_{d-|B|}$ and $U_{d-|C|}$, respectively. These degrees are below $d$, so minimality gives $D_Bf,D_Cf\in K$. The coefficient formula of step 2 shows that their leading exponents are $E-B=C$ and $E-C=B$: all larger monomials of $f$ are additive and killed, while subtracting a fixed multiindex from smaller surviving exponents preserves strict lexicographic order. The displayed binomial coefficients ensure both leading coefficients are nonzero. Since $|B|+|C|=|E|=d$, the two homogeneous degrees sum to $(d-|B|)+(d-|C|)=d$. Their product $g=(D_Bf)(D_Cf)$ therefore lies in $K_d$ and has leading exponent $B+C=E$. Indeed every other product of terms has a strictly smaller exponent, by compatibility of lexicographic order with addition, and the leading coefficient is a product of two nonzero field elements. This is the finite monomial multiplication of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. The normalization of $f$ in step 5 now forces its coefficient at $E$ to vanish, contrary to the choice of $E$.

proof.text: The contradiction rules out a least degree of disagreement. Hence $U_d=K_d$ for every $d$, and the finite homogeneous sums give $U=K=k[T]$. Together with step 1 this proves both assertions.

lean.statement: theorem projective_order_algebra_additive_generators {k : Type u} [Field k] (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (q : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin N) k)) [q.IsPrime] (hq : @Ideal.IsHomogeneous _ _ _ _ _ _ (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin N) k) _ _ MvPolynomial.gradedAlgebra q) (hrel : ¬ @HomogeneousIdeal.toIdeal _ _ _ _ _ _ (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin N) k) _ _ MvPolynomial.gradedAlgebra (@HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin N) k) MvPolynomial.gradedAlgebra) ≤ q) : ∃ U : Subalgebra k (MvPolynomial (Fin N) k), (∀ f : MvPolynomial (Fin N) k, f ∈ U ↔ ∀ d : ℕ, algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin N) k) (Localization.AtPrime q) (MvPolynomial.homogeneousComponent d f) ∈ q.map (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin N) k) (Localization.AtPrime q)) ^ d) ∧ (@Submodule.IsHomogeneous _ _ _ _ _ _ _ U.toSubmodule (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin N) k) _ _ _ MvPolynomial.decomposition) ∧ U = Algebra.adjoin k {t : MvPolynomial (Fin N) k | t ∈ U ∧ (∃ d : ℕ, 0 < d ∧ t.IsHomogeneous d) ∧ MvPolynomial.aeval (fun i : Fin N ↦ (MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inl i) : MvPolynomial (Fin N ⊕ Fin N) k) + MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inr i)) t = MvPolynomial.rename (Sum.inl : Fin N → Fin N ⊕ Fin N) t + MvPolynomial.rename (Sum.inr : Fin N → Fin N ⊕ Fin N) t}
